title: Smart Nursing Home vs Traditional Facility: What Actually Changes
summary: Smart nursing home vs traditional facility: same building, but one can tell you what is happening right now. What actually changes, day by day.
body_text: The difference between a traditional and a smart skilled nursing facility is not the building. It is whether the building can tell you what is happening right now. Same walls, same beds, same staff, but the smart version replaces guessing and hunting with live answers, starting with where the equipment is. That is the whole comparison in one line, and it is worth sitting with, because the phrase "smart facility" makes operators picture a different building. It is not. It is the same building you run today, with a thin layer of awareness laid over it. The traditional version and the smart version look identical from the parking lot. The difference only shows up in the moments when someone needs to know something and cannot find out fast. The stakes are why the gap matters. A typical 110-bed nursing home loses $155,000 to $500,000 a year to equipment waste , and the median skilled nursing facility runs on a roughly 1.8 percent operating margin , so that waste can equal most of a building's annual profit. Most of it leaks through the small daily moments below, the ones a traditional building simply cannot see. Same building, different information Strip away the marketing and the smart version is one thing: real-time operational awareness . In a traditional facility, the answers to basic questions live in people's heads, on paper logs, and in end-of-shift guesses. Where is the bariatric bed the new admit needs this afternoon? Did the rental wheelchair actually come back, or is it still billing? Do we own three of these already, or do we rent another? The traditional building can answer all of these, eventually, by sending someone to look. A smart facility answers them by glancing at a screen. Nothing about the care model changes, and nothing about the building changes. What changes is that the questions stop being "who remembers" and become "look at the map." For the fuller definition of what that layer is and is not, see what a smart skilled nursing facility actually means . It helps to be clear about why the gap exists in the first place, because it is not a discipline problem. A traditional facility loses track of equipment not because the staff are careless, but because the building gives them no way to keep track without stopping care to do it. Every paper log and every "let me go check" is a competent person filling in for information the building does not surface on its own. The smart version does not ask the team to try harder. It removes the reason they had to. A day in each The contrast is easiest to feel through a normal day. None of these moments look like a crisis, which is exactly why they add up to six figures a year: each one is a small tax on time or money that a traditional building has no way to see, repeated across every shift. Here are five of them, run the traditional way and the smart way. A nurse needs a wheelchair for a discharge. In the traditional facility she walks two floors and asks three people. In the smart facility she checks the screen and walks straight to the room it is in. The survey team arrives and asks the administrator to produce the equipment log. Traditionally that kicks off a clipboard hunt, floor by floor, to confirm what is where. In the smart facility it is a one-click audit report, already current. A resident needs a specialty mattress and the floor assumes there is none free, so someone calls the rental supplier. Traditionally the order goes out because no one can confirm otherwise. In the smart facility the screen shows an identical mattress sitting idle upstairs, and the rental is never placed. An expensive pump goes missing. In the traditional building it is noticed weeks later at the next audit, long after the trail goes cold. In the smart facility it surfaces the same day it stops appearing where it should. Month-end arrives and finance reconciles the equipment bill. The traditional facility pays for rentals nobody remembered to send back, because there was no way to see them idling. The smart facility flagged each idle rental on its own, so it went back instead of billing another month. The moment The traditional way The smart way Finding a wheelchair Walk the floors and ask around until one turns up Glance at the live map and go straight to it Prepping for a survey Manual clipboard sweep to confirm what is where One-click audit report, already current Deciding on a rental Order it because no one can confirm you own a free one See the idle unit you already own and skip the rental An item going missing Noticed at the next audit, after the trail is cold Surfaces the same day it stops appearing Month-end costs Pays for rentals nobody remembered to return Idle rentals flagged on their own and sent back Read the left column honestly. It is not neglect, and it is not a bad team. It is what a building without live visibility can do, no matter how good the staff are. Every one of those moments is someone competent working around missing information. The smart column does not add effort, it removes the hunt. Notice too that the smart column never asks anyone to do a new thing. There is no scan to remember, no log to keep current, no step to enforce on a short-staffed floor. The equipment reports its own location, room by room, so the live map stays right whether anyone tends it or not. That is the quiet difference behind all five rows: the traditional way depends on people keeping information current by hand, and the smart way does not depend on anyone at all. What makes the shift affordable now For years the reason operators stayed on the left column was cost. Making a building "smart" used to mean a wired, capital-intensive hospital tracking system, ceiling hardware, a construction schedule, and a bill no SNF margin could justify. That reputation is real, and it belongs to an older generation of technology. The modern version inverts it. A smart facility today is a set of lightweight layers you add to the building you already have, not a project you build into it. Norra's equipment layer is the clearest example: proprietary smart tags attach to equipment in seconds, plug-in gateways sit in an ordinary outlet, and the whole thing delivers room-level location with no upfront capital cost, no wiring, no ceiling installation, no infrastructure buildout, and no staff scanning . It goes live in days, nothing is torn out, and no beds close. That is why the shift is finally affordable for a single building, and why you do not need a renovation to get it. We walk through exactly how in building a smart nursing home without renovation . The economics per building are what changed the math. When a smart facility meant a six-figure capital project, the payback had to be spread across a whole chain and years of use before it penciled out. When it is a plug-in layer with no upfront capital cost, a single 110-bed building that loses six figures a year to equipment waste can justify it on its own, in its first weeks. That is the shift: the thing that used to require the whole organization to say yes now needs only one administrator and one building. Because each layer is additive and reversible, the decision is small. You are not replacing a system or committing a chain. You are adding one layer to one building and keeping it only if it earns its place. You do not flip a switch, you add a layer The move from traditional to smart is not a single switch you throw. It is a first layer you add, and the right first layer is equipment visibility, because it has the fastest payback and asks staff to do nothing. The location updates on its own, so there is no new task, no scanning, and no behavior to enforce on a short-staffed floor. That is what makes it stick when other tools quietly die from disuse. It also means you never have to bet the building on the idea. You add the layer to one facility, watch the same five moments from the table start resolving on a screen instead of in a hunt, and decide from evidence rather than a pitch. If it does not earn its place, you have changed nothing structural and torn nothing out. That reversibility is what makes "become a smart facility" a low-risk move instead of a capital gamble. The results back the sequence. Across a multi-facility skilled nursing network, the equipment layer alone cut equipment spending by as much as 70 percent , saved over 1,100 staff hours per year , and brought unnecessary rentals to zero, with no construction and no new work for staff. Norra is the AI equipment manager built for exactly this layer , and it is the natural place to begin. There is a sequencing wisdom here beyond the money. Starting with a zero-effort layer builds trust before you ask staff or budget for anything harder. When the equipment view simply works, with no training and no new tasks, the team learns that "smart" did not mean "more work," and the next layer becomes an easy yes instead of another fight. Traditional-to-smart is not a leap you take all at once. It is a first layer that earns the second. The through-line is simple. A traditional facility and a smart one can be the same building, run by the same people, on the same day. The only thing that changes is whether they can see what is happening inside it, and that one change is what turns hunting into knowing. If you run skilled nursing and want to see what real-time visibility looks like in your own building, start with a single-facility pilot at norra.io .

title: Best tools to create a business case for a sale (2026)
summary: The best tools to create a business case for a sale in 2026, compared: AI agents that generate the case for you, value-selling platforms, and document builders.
body_text: Last updated: July 2026 The best tools to create a business case for a sale in 2026 are Mutiny, Mediafly, Ecosystems, Cuvama, and PandaDoc. Here is the quick version of who each one is for: Mutiny — best overall for teams that want the full, personalized business case generated for them in minutes and tied to the rest of the deal. Mediafly — best for enterprise value-selling programs run by a dedicated value team. Ecosystems — best when you want the buyer to co-build the value assessment with you. Cuvama — best for tying the value case directly to sales discovery. PandaDoc — best for turning a finished case into a signable proposal document. The biggest difference between these tools is how much of the case each one writes for you. Mutiny generates the problem, the cost of inaction, the ROI, and the narrative for the specific account. The value-selling platforms focus on the ROI math, and the document tools format the final proposal. This guide covers what a business case is, why it decides deals, the types of tools, what to look for, the five best options, and how to generate one. What is a business case in sales? A sales business case is a short, buyer-specific document that justifies a purchase. It states the problem, quantifies the cost of inaction, lays out the proposed solution, and shows the expected ROI and payback for that account. It is the artifact a champion uses to win internal approval, so it has to make the argument on its own without the rep in the room. The business case is also a core component of a deal room, and it often anchors the sales pitch deck. Why does a strong business case matter? A business case decides whether a deal moves or dies, because most buyers require one and most stalled deals stall on justification. Per Forrester, 97% of B2B buyers build a business case to justify their purchases. When the case for change is weak, buyers default to doing nothing: Challenger found that 40% to 60% of lost deals end in no decision rather than a loss to a competitor. The pressure is higher because buyers self-serve. According to Gartner, B2B buyers spend only 17% of the purchase journey with suppliers, and Gartner’s 2025 survey found 61% prefer a rep-free experience. A business case that stands on its own carries the deal through the parts of the journey the rep never sees. Types of business case tools The tools fall into four categories, from most to least hands-off on the actual writing: AI business case generators: create the full, account-specific case (problem, cost of inaction, ROI, and narrative) from your CRM and call context. Mutiny leads here. Value-selling and ROI platforms: quantify ROI and TCO through calculators and value assessments, usually run by a value or enablement team. Mediafly and Ecosystems sit here. Discovery-to-value tools: turn sales discovery into a structured value case. Cuvama sits here. Document and proposal builders: format and e-sign the finished case. PandaDoc sits here. Most categories still leave the rep to write the narrative. The AI generator category is the one that produces a finished, personalized case a champion can forward. What should you look for in a business case tool? Look for four things: how much of the case the tool creates for you, how well it personalizes to the account, whether any rep can use it without a value team, and whether it connects to the rest of the deal. Content generation: does it draft the full case, or only the ROI numbers? Personalization: can it tailor the case to the specific account automatically? Self-serve usability: can any rep build one, or does it need a dedicated value or enablement team? Connected workflow: does the case tie into the deal room, pricing, and follow-ups, or live in a silo? The 5 best tools to create a business case for a sale 1. Mutiny Mutiny is the top-rated AI tool for creating personalized deal content and GTM workflow automation. For business cases, Mutiny generates the whole case itself: the problem, the cost of inaction, the ROI, and the narrative built for the specific account, in minutes. It runs as a two-sided model. The agent creates the customer-facing case, and reps and marketers build their own agents and routines to automate the busywork around the deal, from follow-ups to keeping the numbers current. Any AE, BDR, marketer, or CSM can run it on day one with no GTM engineer or value team required, starting from a pre-built business case blueprint. Sales leaders can standardize that blueprint so every rep runs the same play. Best for: teams that want the full business case generated and tied to the rest of the deal. Pricing: Free, Business, and Enterprise custom plans (starting at $30k). “Generating something in one shot rather than 100 iterations, that’s the [Mutiny] difference.” Basten Heutink, Chief of Staff, Delphi 2. Mediafly Mediafly is a revenue enablement suite with a value-selling module that provides ROI and TCO calculators and business value assessments. It is strong for enterprise value-selling programs, and it is typically run by an enablement or value team that builds and governs the value tools reps use. Best for: enterprise value-selling programs managed by a dedicated value team. 3. Ecosystems Ecosystems is a collaborative value management platform where a seller and buyer build a value assessment together. It formalizes value selling and keeps the quantified value front and center through the deal and into customer success. Best for: teams that want buyers to co-build the value assessment. 4. Cuvama Cuvama is an AI discovery-to-value-case platform that connects sales discovery to a champion-ready value case. It turns what the rep learns in discovery into a structured “why buy, why now, why us” case grounded in ROI. Best for: teams that want the value case tied directly to discovery. 5. PandaDoc PandaDoc is a document and proposal platform with e-signature. It is useful for turning a finished business case into a polished, signable document, with templates and approval workflows on the contract side of the deal. Best for: turning the business case into a signable proposal document. Tool Best for Approach to the business case Mutiny Generating the full case and connecting it to the deal AI drafts the problem, cost of inaction, ROI, and narrative per account; reps automate the surrounding workflow Mediafly Enterprise value-selling programs ROI and TCO calculators run by a value team Ecosystems Buyer-collaborative value selling Value assessments co-built with the buyer Cuvama Discovery-driven value cases Connects discovery to a champion-ready value case PandaDoc Signable proposal documents Document templates and e-signature How do you generate a business case for a sale? At a high level: state the problem in the buyer’s words, quantify the cost of inaction, lay out the solution, show the ROI with clear assumptions, and end with a recommendation and next step. For the step-by-step walkthrough, see how to build a business case for a B2B deal, or start from a business case template. For the component list, see what a sales business case should include. The fastest path is to generate the case rather than write it by hand. With Mutiny, a rep starts from the business case blueprint and the agent generates the personalized case in minutes, so the first draft exists before the rep would otherwise have finished the math. See how account executives use Mutiny to build deal-ready cases without waiting on a value team.

title: What Is an International Payment Gateway? A Beginner’s Guide
summary: Learn how a payment gateway for international payments works, how to accept international payments in India, key features to compare, and how to choose the right solution for your business.
body_text: Table of Contents Toggle Expanding your business globally means making it easy for overseas customers to pay you. Whether you’re a freelancer, exporter, SaaS company, or ecommerce brand, you’ll need a payment gateway for international payments to securely accept transactions from customers across different countries and currencies. An international payment gateway does more than process payments. It enables businesses to accept international cards, supports multiple currencies, handles currency conversion, and complies with both Indian and global payment regulations. With the right solution, Indian businesses can sell globally while offering a seamless checkout experience. But what an international payment gateway is, how it works, its key features, and what to consider when choosing the best payment gateway for international transactions. Let’s break it all down. What Are International Transactions? International transactions refer to the exchange of goods, services, or funds between individuals or businesses in different countries. For example, an Indian exporter shipping products to Europe, a SaaS company billing customers in the US, or a freelancer receiving payments from clients overseas are all examples of international transactions. Unlike domestic payments, cross-border transactions involve multiple currencies, banking networks, exchange rates, and country-specific regulations. A reliable payment gateway to accept international payments in India simplifies these complexities by securely processing payments, managing currency conversion, and ensuring regulatory compliance. What Is an International Payment Gateway? An international payment gateway is a secure online payment system that enables businesses to accept and process transactions from customers across the globe. Unlike a domestic gateway that only supports local cards and currency, an international gateway is designed for cross-border commerce. Accept payments in multiple currencies Process international debit and credit cards Support global wallets and payment methods Handle currency conversion Meet RBI and international compliance requirements Settle payments directly into an Indian bank account In short, it enables Indian businesses to accept payments from customers worldwide while delivering a secure and frictionless payment experience. How Does a Payment Gateway for International Payments Work? When an overseas customer makes a purchase from your website, an international payment gateway securely processes the transaction behind the scenes. Here’s how the process works: Customer Checkout: The customer selects a product or service and pays using an international credit card, debit card, or supported digital wallet. Payment Authorization: The payment gateway encrypts the transaction details and securely sends them to the customer’s issuing bank for approval. Currency Conversion: If the customer pays in a foreign currency, the gateway processes the exchange rate and converts the amount before settlement. Transaction Approval: Once the issuing bank verifies the payment, the transaction is approved or declined based on available funds and security checks. Settlement: The approved payment is processed through international banking networks and settled into the merchant’s Indian bank account, usually within a few business days. Reporting & Compliance: The gateway provides transaction reports, settlement details, and required documentation to help businesses manage accounting and regulatory requirements. The entire process takes only a few seconds for customers while ensuring secure and compliant cross-border payment processing . Common Types of International Payments Businesses use international payment gateways for a variety of cross-border transactions, including: Retail and Service Sales: E-commerce, consulting, software, all billed globally. Education and Events: Online tutoring, webinars, and digital courses with overseas participants. Subscription and SaaS: Monthly or annual plans for clients abroad. Remittances: Individuals sending money for personal or family needs. Export payments Whether you’re selling physical products or digital services, an international payment gateway helps streamline payment collection from customers worldwide. Key Features of an International Payment Gateway When evaluating a payment gateway for international payments, look for these essential features: Multi-Currency Support: The payment system should be capable of accepting payments in over 100 global currencies; this way, customers can pay in the currency they are most comfortable with. Meanwhile, your dashboard displays the settled INR or the currency of your choice. Wide, Ranging Payment Methods: The platform should facilitate the use of international cards (Visa, MasterCard, Amex), global wallets (PayPal, Apple Pay), and the alternative payment methods that are most relevant to the buyers residing overseas. Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) : Allow customers to specify their home currency and make payments with full transparency, thereby lessening the points of contact and increasing the chances of getting conversions. Localized Checkout: A checkout process would be more efficient with local language support, allowing the checkout pages to appear in the language of the local consumers, coupled with local checkout patterns. PCI DSS & Global Security Compliance: The presence of end to end encryption, tokenization, & 3D secure features assists in securing each & every transaction. Fraud Detection: Smarter anti-fraud tools, fueled by Artificial Intelligence, and flexible risk engines that have learned from global trends. Developer, Friendly Integration: Well-equipped with APIs, SDKs, plug-and-play modules for the most popular commerce stacks, such as Shopify, WooCommerce, amongst others. Real Time Analytics: Combined dashboards which give real insights into real processes of sales & reconcilements in domestic as well as international refunds. Instant Onboarding and No-Code Tools: From your own dashboard, the ability to immediately start accepting payments worldwide without the hassle of complicated coding and paperwork is possible. These features help businesses provide a secure, reliable, and seamless payment experience for customers across different countries. Common Challenges of Accepting International Payments ​​Expanding abroad carries real obstacles, such as prolonged settlement cycles, losses during foreign currency exchange, complicated regulations, or the danger of fraud and/or chargeback losses. Visionary international gateways mitigate such issues by: Providing T+2 or T+3 settlement cycles, so companies get payments faster. Fixing transparent and competitive exchange rates accessible to both buyers and sellers Making FIRS & compliance processes automated for peace of mind Applying universal anti-fraud techniques in all transactions This helps businesses, individuals, and young entrepreneurs to venture easily into other markets without worrying about any limitations being created either technologically or financially. Integrating an International Payment Gateway Modern payment gateways are designed for businesses of all sizes, making integration simple even without extensive technical expertise. Most providers offer: Plugins for Shopify , WooCommerce, Magento, and other ecommerce platforms APIs and SDKs for custom websites and mobile apps No-code payment links and hosted checkout pages Dashboards to manage settlements, refunds, and reports This allows businesses to start accepting international payments quickly while delivering a smooth checkout experience. How to Choose the Best Payment Gateway for International Transactions Entering new markets around the world generates new income sources; however, there are also new complexities, particularly regarding securing funds more quickly. Choosing the international payment gateway has to integrate properly with how people pay in different countries around the world and how you want to manage your operations in the background. Here are a few key factors to help guide the decision: Coverage of Currencies and Local Payment Options: Customers are more likely to complete purchases when they can pay in their own currency and use familiar methods. A good gateway should support multi-currency transactions and give access to local payment options. This can include cards, e-wallets, and money transfer solutions that are common practice within a certain region. For example, support for UPI in India or SEPA in Europe can make a noticeable difference in conversion rates. Global Compliance and Regulatory Alignment: International payments are processed under various taxation laws and privacy regulations, and protection against fraud in each country. Look for a provider that handles regional compliance requirements like PSD2, SCA, and local tax calculations, so you don’t run into trouble managing cross-border transactions. Fraud Protection and Risk Tools: Global payments bring higher fraud exposure, so built-in protection is key. Look for gateways with real-time detection, adaptive risk scoring, and customizable rules. Cashfree offers RiskShield , which helps flag suspicious disbursals using pattern analysis and rule-based filters. It’s especially useful for businesses managing vendor payouts or high-volume transactions. Transparent Pricing and Fee Structure: International transactions will have extra charges for things like currency exchange fees and international card network fees. Be sure to ask for a full quotation of the charges involved. Compare the charges of the payment services when it comes to refund charges, chargeback fees , and the time taken for payouts. Cashfree— International Payment Gateway for Ambitious Indian Brands While the world of payment gateways is crowded, a few have built deep expertise specifically focused on Indian businesses scaling into global markets. Cashfree stands out with its suite of cross-border solutions, built to offer the features growing ventures actually need. Broad Currency Support: Supports payments in 140+ currencies, with settlement in Card and leading International Wallets automatically in Indian Rupees. This enables the merchant to forget the troubles of conversion and give the foreign customer a seamless experience. Seamless Onboarding Process: The activation process of KYC and compliance requirements is made easy for Indian merchants. It takes just one day with only digital processes involved. You can go global in hours instead of weeks. Unified Dashboard: Manage both domestic and international sales from a single platform, including analytics, refunds, FIRS, and settlement data. Dynamic Currency Conversion: Cashfree’s “Pay Native” lets your international buyers always see transparent rates and pay in their home currency. Compliance and Security: PCI DSS level 1, advanced risk management, and strong fraud checks ensure every transaction is protected according to the world’s best standards. 24/7 Support: A dedicated support team is available for troubleshooting, disputes, and compliance guidance, bridging time zones as your business grows globally. Thousands of Indian startups, exporters, D2C businesses, and SaaS companies have already utilized the international payment gateway provided by Cashfree to access a fresh set of markets for increased conversions and revenue streams without the usual operational burden of weeks of effort. Conclusion The push for cross-border payments isn’t just for the world’s biggest brands. Every Indian company, regardless of size or stage, now has the infrastructure to serve buyers from San Francisco to Singapore, all thanks to international payment gateways that make complexity invisible. Knowing what a payment gateway is in India, and selecting one with global capability, is the first step toward international growth. Ready to Accept International Payments? Expand your business globally with a secure payment gateway that supports multiple currencies, international cards, and seamless cross-border transactions – all from one platform. Start Accepting International Payments Frequently Asked Questions What is an international payment gateway? An international payment gateway enables businesses to accept online payments from customers in different countries using multiple currencies, international cards, and global payment methods. How can I accept international payments in India? You can accept international payments by integrating a payment gateway that supports cross-border transactions, international cards, multi-currency processing, and RBI-compliant settlements. How do I get paid in INR if my customer pays in USD or EUR? The gateway locks in an exchange rate at the point of checkout. Once the payment made abroad gets settled, the equivalent Indian rupees will be directly transferred to your Indian bank account without the need to deal with the forex. Is it safe to accept international payments online? “Yes. International gateways adhere to compliance of PCI DSS worldwide, employ advanced encryption, and use anti-fraud engines to ensure every transaction is secure.” What documents are needed to start accepting international payments? Usually, the essential KYC documents, such as GSTIN, PAN, and bank accounts, would be required. In export-oriented units, export registration could also be mandatory. Can freelancers or small businesses use international payment gateways? Yes, today’s gateways like Cashfree are designed for every business size, from a solo freelancer to large D2C operations, making it easy to bill and receive payments from clients worldwide. How long do international payment settlements take? Settlement timelines vary by provider and destination country but typically range from 2 to 5 business days.

title: Netskope Slashes Network Latency By Up to 90% for Enterprise AI Traffic
summary: Enhanced AI-specific peering and intelligent route optimizations from the Netskope NewEdge Network secure AI without performance trade-offs SANTA CLARA,
body_text: Enhanced AI-specific peering and intelligent route optimizations from the Netskope NewEdge Network secure AI without performance trade-offs SANTA CLARA, Calif. – July 21, 2026 – Netskope (NASDAQ: NTSK), a leader in modern security and networking for the cloud and AI era, today announced performance results derived from continued innovations of its NewEdge AI Fast Path technology. Part of the Netskope NewEdge private cloud, AI Fast Path optimizes the network path between users, sites, and agents to AI destinations for faster inference results and minimizing time to first token (TTFT), accelerating complex multi-prompt agentic AI workflows, as well as optimizing LLM performance when accessing large volumes of data. In testing performed across the NewEdge global network with real-world traffic, AI Fast Path was shown to reduce latency by as much as 90% to popular AI destinations. More than 80% [1] of infrastructure and operations (I&O) leaders today aren’t confident that their current team and budget can meet the intensifying network performance, resilience, and security demands of the AI era. Through the combination of extensive peering and continuous, automated route optimization, AI Fast Path is shown to significantly reduce latency for AI traffic, giving enterprises fast, secure access to AI without the performance trade-offs common to approaches that rely on the public internet or third-party infrastructure. “Netskope’s optimizations strip away network overhead associated with AI, which compounds as traffic shifts from simple inference to complex agentic workflows,” said Frank Dickson, Group Vice President, Security & Trust, IDC. “By eliminating latency, NewEdge AI Fast Path also protects against costly GPUs sitting idle, wasting money, and creating compute bottlenecks.” Turning network telemetry into AI-ready performance Netskope security, network, and AI services are delivered by Netskope NewEdge, a private cloud infrastructure consisting of more than 120 data centers in over 80 regions worldwide. Every NewEdge data center is designed to offer full compute and all Netskope services, including Netskope One SASE and Netskope One AI Security . As of June 2026, NewEdge maintains more than 12,000 network adjacencies to over 750 unique autonomous system numbers (ASNs), including direct peering relationships with leading AI destinations. This peering density ranks NewEdge among the largest networks in the world by global Internet Exchange (IX) participation, alongside hyperscale networks including AWS, Google, and Microsoft [2] . Available to Netskope customers as part of the Netskope One platform, AI Fast Path brings together the NewEdge network’s extensive peering with its unique Route Control technology that continuously analyzes network conditions. Every day, NewEdge analyzes tens of millions of routes, evaluating latency, jitter, and packet loss to identify the fastest, most reliable path, and automatically shifting traffic when a better path becomes available. In addition, AI Fast Path takes into account measurements specific to AI traffic, including TTFT, sustained token generation rate, time per output token (TPOT), the percentage of total AI latency attributable to network roundtrip time, and other factors related to AI provider response times or geographic variations. AI Fast Path improves AI performance for customers, and bolsters network resilience and availability even with unexpected events that could trigger route changes, which might include: Internet “weather” events, such as traffic spikes Congestion ISP connectivity failures, such as fiber cuts AI provider infrastructure or cloud outages In each case, Route Control automatically routes around the disruption, helping maintain a consistent digital experience for users, sites, and agents interacting with AI applications even when the underlying internet is not cooperating. In some of the most demanding AI use cases (such as a high-speed financial trading application, medical scan detecting a life-threatening anomaly or smart sensor triggering a security alert) such routing can also prevent catastrophic impacts “Every AI workflow, whether it’s a person prompting a chatbot or an autonomous agent chaining together a dozen calls to an LLM, is only as fast as the network performance underneath it,” said Joe DePalo, Chief Platform Officer, Netskope. “Netskope is recognized as a market leader not only for AI security, but also for the network performance that underpins successful AI workflows. Thanks to NewEdge, our customers meet their need for AI speed without adding unnecessary risks or affecting the user experience.” About Netskope Netskope (NASDAQ: NTSK), a leader in modern security and networking for the cloud and AI era, addresses the needs of both security and networking teams by providing optimized access and real-time, context-based security for the AI ecosystem inclusive of agents, applications, tools, LLMs, people, devices, and data. Thousands of customers, including more than 30% of the Fortune 100, trust the Netskope One platform, its Zero Trust Engine, and its powerful NewEdge network to reduce risk and gain full visibility and control over cloud, AI, SaaS, web, and private applications — providing security and accelerating performance without trade-offs. Learn more at netskope.com , on LinkedIn , and on Instagram . Media Relations Contact: [email protected] Investor Relations Contact: [email protected] Methodology note: Route Control and NewEdge Traffic Management figures reflect NewEdge telemetry collected June 5–12, 2026. The up-to-90% latency reduction claim reflects testing to a representative AI destination from a single NewEdge data center during the same period; exact results may vary by location, destination, and network conditions. AI-specific performance measurements (TTFT, TPOT, throughput, network fraction, P95/P90 ratio, geographic COV) are currently derived from synthetic, ongoing monitoring of AI provider endpoints. body_text: A tragic wildlife incident in Indonesia has drawn global attention after a man was reportedly killed by a large reticulated python while walking home alone at night. The incident, which happened in North Maluku, has renewed discussions about human safety in areas where people live close to natural habitats. According to local reports, the victim, identified as 35-year-old Hasim Lumbessy, disappeared after leaving a rural gathering in the early hours of the morning. Residents later discovered evidence of a snake attack along a forested path, leading to the recovery of his body from inside a large python. While such incidents are extremely rare, experts say they highlight the importance of understanding wildlife behaviour, especially in tropical regions where large snakes are naturally found. Man Reportedly Killed by Large Python in North Maluku Reports from Indonesia stated that Hasim Lumbessy was walking home alone at approximately 3am when he was attacked in a forested area of North Maluku. The region contains extensive woodland and agricultural areas, where encounters between humans and wildlife can occur. After Hasim failed to return home, relatives and local residents began searching for him. During the search, villagers reportedly found personal belongings, including bags and sandals, along with signs that suggested a struggle had taken place. Authorities said the search continued near Fatliwangka Road, where residents discovered a large python with an unusually swollen body. The snake was later examined, and villagers reportedly found the victim inside. The incident shocked the local community and led police officials to remind residents to take extra precautions when travelling through forest areas. Police Issue Warning After Fatal Snake Encounter Following the incident, local authorities encouraged people living near forest environments to avoid walking alone in areas where dangerous wildlife may be present. Police officials advised residents who need to enter woodland areas or remote locations to travel with others whenever possible. They also highlighted the importance of staying alert, particularly during early morning or nighttime hours when visibility is reduced. North Maluku is home to diverse wildlife, and officials stressed that forests remain natural habitats for many species, including large snakes. The warning comes as communities continue to balance everyday activities, farming, and travel with the need to respect surrounding ecosystems. Why Reticulated Pythons Can Become Dangerous Reticulated pythons are among the longest snakes in the world. They are native to Southeast Asia and are known for their impressive size, strength, and ability to survive in different environments. These snakes are non-venomous, meaning they do not use poison to kill prey. Instead, they rely on powerful muscles to constrict their targets. Once a python has successfully captured prey, its body strength can prevent the victim from escaping. Although large pythons are capable of attacking humans, experts explain that such events are uncommon. Most snakes avoid humans and prefer to remain hidden when possible. Attacks generally occur when a snake feels threatened, is surprised, or sees an opportunity for food. Habitat changes, reduced forest areas, and increased human activity in wildlife zones can increase the possibility of encounters. Previous Python Incidents in Indonesia The latest case follows other reported python-related deaths in Indonesia, particularly in areas where villages and forests are closely connected. In previous incidents, residents in North Maluku and other regions reported deadly encounters involving very large pythons. These cases have attracted international attention because attacks of this nature are rarely documented. Indonesia’s tropical environment provides suitable conditions for reticulated pythons. The country’s forests contain abundant wildlife, creating natural feeding opportunities for large predators. However, experts caution against assuming that every large snake is a threat. Most snakes play an important role in controlling populations of smaller animals and maintaining ecological balance. Expert Advice on Staying Safe Around Pythons Wildlife specialists say prevention is one of the best ways to reduce risks in areas where large snakes live. People travelling through forested locations should consider the following safety measures: • Avoid walking alone in isolated areas, especially after dark. • Carry a torch when travelling through areas with limited visibility. • Stay on recognised paths rather than entering dense vegetation unnecessarily. • Be cautious near rivers, farmland, and areas where animals may gather. • Avoid approaching or attempting to handle large snakes. Experts also advise people not to panic if they encounter a snake. Sudden movements or attempts to capture the animal can increase the risk of an aggressive response. The Importance of Respecting Wildlife Habitats Human and animal encounters are becoming more common in some regions because communities are expanding into areas that were previously dominated by forests. Conservation experts often emphasise that protecting natural habitats benefits both wildlife and people. Healthy ecosystems allow animals to maintain their natural behaviour while reducing unexpected contact with humans. Education is another important factor. Communities that understand local wildlife are better prepared to avoid dangerous situations and respond appropriately during encounters. Large snakes may appear frightening, but they are also important parts of tropical ecosystems. Their role includes controlling populations of rodents and other animals that can affect agriculture and human health. Conclusion The reported death of Hasim Lumbessy in North Maluku is a rare and tragic reminder of the challenges faced by communities living alongside powerful wildlife. While reticulated python attacks on humans remain extremely uncommon, the incident highlights the need for awareness, caution, and respect for natural habitats. Authorities continue to encourage residents and visitors to take sensible precautions when entering forest areas. Understanding wildlife behaviour and following safety advice can help reduce risks while allowing humans and animals to coexist. title: DoorDash Integrates Directly with Shopify to Connect Brick-and-Mortar Retailers with On-Demand Delivery
summary: A first-of-its-kind integration lets independent retailers get their products to consumers on demand — launching in the U.S., with international expansion planned in the months ahead.
body_text: Local businesses are the backbone of their communities. Today, we're making it easier than ever for them to reach consumers nearby. DoorDash is announcing an integration that gives independent Shopify retailers a direct, seamless path to integrate with DoorDash through the tools they already use every day. In our recent Economic Impact Report, 90% of merchants say DoorDash has helped them reach new consumers they otherwise wouldn't have been able to reach, while 85% of consumers say DoorDash makes it easier to support local businesses in their community. DoorDash is now available as a native sales channel inside Shopify's App Store — meaning any Shopify merchants with a brick-and-mortar presence in the US can add their product catalog to the DoorDash marketplace by enabling a new channel, with no separate onboarding process, manual catalog uploads, or disruption to existing operations. For consumers, this means more local stores and more delivery options in your neighborhood, available on demand. "If it's in your area, it's on DoorDash. That's the promise driving today's news. Local, independent retailers are the heart of local commerce, and they deserve tools that work as hard as they do," said Mike Goldblatt, Vice President of Enterprise Partnerships at DoorDash. "As the first on-demand marketplace that Shopify merchants can activate directly from their existing Shopify Admin, we're opening the door to retail merchants who can now reach their communities faster than ever." “Merchants want to sell wherever their customers are, and increasingly that means meeting them with speed and convenience,” said Atlee Clark, Vice President of Partnerships at Shopify. "This integration puts local retailers in front of millions of DoorDash shoppers and turns same-day demand into sales, all managed inside Shopify.” For retailers: Merchants keep their existing workflow. No changes to existing workflows. Shopify merchants extend their reach to DoorDash consumers without leaving the platform they already rely on. Go live in days, not weeks: Self-serve integration onboarding is built directly into the Shopify experience, cutting setup time from weeks to days. Products and inventory stay in sync automatically — so when a customer orders, what's on DoorDash always matches what's on the shelf. No duplicate data entry, no manual updates when stock changes. Merchants manage their catalog in Shopify, and it reflects on DoorDash in real time, keeping products moving to customers as fast as possible. From a neighborhood gift shop and a local sporting goods store to a specialty food retailer, local businesses can now tap into on-demand delivery and discovery on DoorDash without the operational burden that used to come with it. This partnership means real impact for merchants and local communities. Install the DoorDash Sales Channel App here .
